Probe: the new test file against main's code fails at collection (ModuleNotFoundError ddflow.api.constellation); against the branch 22 pass; the data kind loads through templates/kinds (tests/test_kind_data_packaged.py, 198 related tests pass) and the command is placed as action constellation of ddflow_admin. Read D-constellation, D-multirepo-answers, CN-decide body, R-constellation recall.

Checked r-extension-contract (kind declared as data in templates/kinds, no hub edit; command auto-discovered), r-record-parity (CLI, one action of ddflow_admin, prompt in help topic constellation), r-everything-configurable ([constellation] knobs in config_sections), r-feature-four-ways (file, config, CLI/MCP, prompt), r-company-workflows (help page overridable, knobs per project/org), r-adapters (TOML via adapters.toml, writes via infra.fsio.replace_text), r-small-files (all new files under 8 KB), r-safe-by-default (trust external, credential remotes refused, manifest path confined to the project), r-replay-compat (reuses existing def.* events, no new event kind), r-docs-with-the-change (docs/guide/constellation.md, cli-mcp.md, help topic, 4 knob upgrade fragments).

chunk_findings.detail: `member_add` builds a member `fields` mapping that includes `notes`, but it records only `CC.Member(**fields).fields()` through `_put`. The surrounding code treats `notes` as separate from `fields()` (`_row` and `_agrees` use `m.fields() | {"notes": m.notes}`, and `member_edit`'s live-record path passes `member.fields() | {"notes": member.notes}`), so `_put` stores a record without the `notes` key. For `ddflow constellation add --name alpha --remote https://x --role provider --notes "owner: alice"`, the record log lacks `notes`; `member_list` then puts the member in `out_of_step` because `_agrees` compares the stored record (missing `notes`) with the file member's redacted note, and history/search/RAG export of the member omit the note.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/constellation.py:member_add / _put

chunk_findings.detail: `member_remove` only retires a record when `known is not None and known.live`. If a member exists in `.ddflow/constellation.toml` but has no live record (an out-of-step state the API itself exposes via `recorded: false` and `out_of_step`), the function skips any record call, deletes the file entry, and returns `O.ok`. Example: manually add an `alpha` entry to the manifest with no corresponding record, then run `ddflow constellation remove --name alpha --reason cleanup`; the file changes and the call succeeds, but no `def.retired` tombstone/event is recorded, so `ddflow constellation history alpha` and replay restore do not show the removal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/constellation.py:member_remove

chunk_findings.detail: When a conflict or unrestorable member exists but nothing needs to be written, `member_sync` returns an `O.nothing` outcome whose message begins `"the log and the manifest agree"` even though `_agree_note` has just reported a disagreement. For example, if the manifest still lists member `alpha` while the corresponding record is a tombstone, `_record_entries` puts `alpha` in `conflicts`, `recorded`/`updated`/`restored` are empty, and the final message becomes `"the log and the manifest agree; alpha retired in the log but still in the file"`. The log and manifest do not agree, so the message is factually wrong and can cause an agent or CLI that trusts the message to treat a conflict as agreement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/constellation_sync.py:member_sync

chunk_findings.detail: `_manifest_path` is documented as enforcing that the manifest stays inside the project, but it misses Windows absolute paths that begin with a backslash. It only rejects values starting with `/` or `~`, and it catches drive letters only when `v[1] == ":"`. Given a Windows environment and config value `manifest = "\outside\constellation.toml"` (a single leading backslash), the function returns no error: `v.startswith(("/", "~"))` is false, the normalized split contains no `..` component, and `v[1]` is not `:`. If the manifest path is later joined to the project root with normal path semantics, the leading backslash resolves to an absolute path outside the project, so the check fails to enforce its stated invariant.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/constellation.py:_manifest_path

chunk_findings.detail: The control-character check explicitly exempts newline from the forbidden set, so it permits newlines inside `remote`. That lets the credential check at `_CREDENTIAL.match(remote.strip())` be bypassed: for an entry such as `{"name": "x", "remote": "https: [REDACTED]host", "role": "provider", "trust": "own"}`, `problem` returns `""` because the newline is not rejected and the regex cannot match the userinfo across the whitespace. `from_table` then creates a `Member` whose `remote` still contains the credential, and `render` writes it into the committed manifest (escaped as `\n`). This defeats the intended protection against committing credentials in the manifest.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/constellation.py:problem (control-character check near line 82)

chunk_findings.detail: The file’s own docstring says the MCP entry is only an action of the `ddflow_admin` family and must not add a tool of its own, but the command is declared with `tool="ddflow_constellation"` and exported via `BY_TOOL`. If the MCP surface enumerates `BY_TOOL` (as the export name and family/action pattern imply), this adds a separate `ddflow_constellation` MCP tool, contrary to the stated design and the “tools list is paid for in every session” constraint.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/constellation.py:60 (`tool="ddflow_constellation"`)

chunk_findings.detail: The help page documents that the event log redacts text shaped like an e-mail address, which includes valid SSH remotes such as `[REDACTED:email]:org/specs.git`, and then states that if the manifest file is lost such a member is “added again, not restored.” Since `remote` is a required field in the kind template (`ddflow/templates/kinds/constellation_member.toml:29`), a member created with the documented MCP example (`remote=[REDACTED:email]:org/specs.git`) cannot be faithfully replayed/restored from its event history: the required remote is missing or altered in the log. This makes `ddflow constellation sync` restore lossy for SSH remotes and violates the record contract’s logged-events/replay-restore guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/constellation.md:27-29

chunk_findings.detail: The guide documents that a member remote such as its own example `[REDACTED:email]:org/specs.git` is redacted in the event log and that `sync` will not restore that member from the log. Given the documented workflow, a user can add the example SSH remote, later lose or accidentally delete that live member from the committed manifest, and then find that replay/`sync` cannot reconstruct it because the remote was treated as e-mail-shaped redacted text. This contradicts the stated conformance requirement that every record kind has logged events and replay restore [D-universal-principles]; a non-secret SSH remote is being made unrecoverable from the record history.
chunk_findings.title: docs/guide/constellation.md:16,39-40

chunk_findings.detail: The guide says a project may belong to several constellations by listing the same member `name` under each constellation, but the CLI examples identify members only by name (`edit specs`, `remove specs`, `history specs`) and never show a constellation selector. If `.ddflow/constellation.toml` contains two live members named `specs`, one under `constellation = "payments"` and one under the default constellation, the documented command `ddflow constellation remove specs` cannot unambiguously address the intended member; the documented interface cannot support the documented multi-constellation use without guessing or erroring.
chunk_findings.title: docs/guide/constellation.md:23,29-32

chunk_findings.detail: The smoke test now uses `kind.title` as if it were the name of the kind’s primary field, but `Kind.title` is the kind’s display title, not a field key. For existing data kinds this makes the assertion look up a non-existent field (for example `shown["fields"]["Requirement"]` instead of `shown["fields"]["title"]`), raising `KeyError`, and the subsequent edit sends `{kind.title: "t2"}` as an invalid field name, so `record_edit` fails. The previous hardcoded `"title"` was the field name; supporting `constellation_member` requires an explicit title-field property or a valid title field in the kind’s minimal fields, not reusing the kind’s display title.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_kind_data_packaged.py:50

chunk_findings.detail: Adding a member with notes records the member without the notes. `_put` is called with `CC.Member(**fields).fields()`, but the rest of this module treats `Member.fields()` as not containing `notes`: `_row` explicitly adds `"notes": m.notes`, `member_edit` explicitly passes `member.fields() | {"notes": member.notes}`, and `_agrees` compares the stored `notes` field. So `member_add(..., notes="important")` stores a record whose `notes` is missing/empty, and a subsequent `member_list` puts that member in `out_of_step` because `_agrees` sees `stored.get("notes", "") == ""` instead of `"important"`; the member’s history also lacks the note.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/constellation.py:member_add

chunk_findings.detail: `data["restored"]` is populated by `_restorable` before the manifest file is actually written. If `_record_entries` or `_restorable` returns any failure, or if `write(...)` later raises, `member_sync` returns `_fail(..., **data)` without having successfully written the manifest, but the failure outcome still advertises the `_restorable` ids as `restored`. For example, if the log contains two live member records and the manifest file lacks both, one valid and one invalid, `_restorable` returns `restored=[valid_id]` and `failed=[invalid_id]`; because `failed` is non-empty, the function returns failure before calling `write`, so `valid_id` was not restored into the file, yet the outcome says it was. The same false `restored` list is returned if `write` fails with `OSError` or `ManifestError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/constellation_sync.py:member_sync

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest-path validation claims the manifest “must stay inside the project: a relative path with no '..'”, but it only rejects paths that start with `/` or `~`. It does not reject Windows absolute or UNC paths that start with backslashes, even though the same function explicitly treats backslashes as path separators via `v.replace("\\", "/")`. For example, `_manifest_path(r"\Windows\System32\config\SAM")` returns `""`, marking the config valid, while `Path(project_root) / r"\Windows\System32\config\SAM"` on Windows resolves to the absolute path outside the project. A UNC path such as `r"\\server\share\constellation.toml"` is also accepted by this check. That defeats the knob’s stated “never outside it” guarantee and lets a project-local config point the manifest at arbitrary local or network paths.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/constellation.py:18

chunk_findings.detail: `problem` allows newline in `remote` and does not reject other whitespace, but `_CREDENTIAL` cannot match a URL userinfo that contains whitespace. For example, `from_table({"constellation": "c", "name": "n", "remote": "https: [REDACTED]host", "role": "provider", "trust": "own"}, default_name="c", default_trust="own")` (or the same remote with a space instead of the newline) passes validation because the newline is explicitly excluded from the control-character check and the credential regex fails when whitespace appears before the `@`. `render` then writes the value into the committed manifest, so a credential can be stored despite the stated credential check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/constellation.py:problem

chunk_findings.detail: The help states that the event log redacts text shaped like an e-mail address and that an ssh remote such as `[REDACTED:email]:org/specs.git` is therefore kept whole only in `.ddflow/constellation.toml`; if the file is lost, a member with such a remote is “added again, not restored.” Given the documented add `remote=[REDACTED:email]:org/specs.git`, the recorded event cannot faithfully restore or show the required `remote` value, so `history`/`sync`/replay cannot restore the original record. This violates the stated record contract that every change is a logged event with replay restore [r-everything-managed].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/constellation.md:27

chunk_findings.detail: The guide says each change is an event and that history/search/recall work, but then states the log redacts e-mail-shaped text and `sync` does not restore such a member from the log. The guide’s own example uses `remote = "[REDACTED:email]:org/specs.git"` (line 16), which is e-mail-shaped. Given that documented `add`, the event log contains a redacted remote, so replay/restore or sync-from-log cannot reconstruct the member. This violates the record contract requirement that every change be a logged event with replay restore [D-universal-principles].
chunk_findings.title: docs/guide/constellation.md:38

chunk_findings.detail: `test_the_generic_record_surface_reads_members_and_search_finds_them` never exercises search. It only calls `ddflow record constellation_member list` and asserts the member name appears in the list output. If the `constellation_member` kind is not indexed for search, or the search path returns no hits, this test still passes, so it gives false assurance for the search part of the record contract.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_constellation_manifest.py:230

chunk_findings.detail: `test_the_knobs_exist_with_safe_defaults` calls `Config.load()` with no isolated project/monkeypatch. That asserts the effective ambient config, not the shipped defaults. If the tests are run in a checkout or user home containing a `.ddflow/config.toml` (or other loaded user config) with, for example, `[constellation] default_trust = "own"` or `max_members = 0`, `Config.load()` will pick up the override and the assertions fail even though the shipped defaults are correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_constellation_manifest.py:166

Needs a policy for repository addresses, or an allowlist for field kinds that hold them.
